question: Does task-aligned rank-two depth fusion preserve AUC at lower OCBE parameter count than dense hidden-128 fusion?

runs.timing_note: Exact start time was not captured; ended_at is the output file modification time.
runs.data_split: normal training frames only; 16 evenly spaced frames per scene
normal training frames per scene; paired test video frames and labels
runs.analysis_command: /home/lyx/miniconda3/envs/DMAD/bin/python scripts/summarize_ocbe.py --experiment experiments/da/appearance/20261013_ocbe_depthrank2_hidden128_s42 --comparison width192=experiments/da/appearance/20261012_student_width192_glll_s42 --comparison dense128=experiments/da/appearance/20261013_ocbe_hidden128_dense_s42 --label "OCBE 三层组内深度秩 2 融合"
runs.archive_note: Seven per-frame score CSVs were converted from CRLF to LF after the run for Git; row counts and AUCs were reverified unchanged. Summary CSV was written with LF.

result_summary: Seven-scene macro frame AUC=82.73511733 versus original width-192 OCBE AUC=82.53810786 (delta=+0.19700947 pp) and dense hidden-128 AUC=82.61367738 (delta=+0.12143995 pp); OCBE+student trainable parameters=3,761,216, down 51.27% versus original and 9.46% versus dense hidden-128. Crossroads declines 1.27972638 pp versus dense; seed 42 only.
limitations: The discarded within-group depth-curvature direction may contain anomaly-relevant information.
Normal-feature projection energy does not establish anomaly AUC.
Macro AUC differences of +0.1970 and +0.1214 pp are too small to claim a reliable gain without multi-seed replication.
Crossroads and Vehicle decline 1.2797 and 1.0173 pp versus dense hidden-128, respectively.
Normal-feature depth energy was measured before training without learned LayerNorm affine parameters and does not guarantee anomaly discrimination.
Target UAV end-to-end latency was not measured.
